title: Thi chuẩn hóa và năng lực thật · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support reducing the role of standardised examinations in school assessment, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Dạng discuss yêu cầu giải thích riêng vì sao mỗi phía tin lập trường của mình rồi đưa phán đoán của người viết. Trong bài này, cân nhắc trọng tâm là: Dự án kéo dài để lộ quá trình tìm nguồn, sửa lập luận và quản lý công việc mà bài thi ngắn khó thấy. Đây là thay đổi thứ được đo, không đơn giản làm đánh giá dễ hơn. Chấm của giáo viên khác nhau khiến cùng năng lực nhận điểm khác nhau. Điều tiết chấm bên ngoài tăng tính so sánh; một phần thi chung giữ mốc đối chiếu, nên bài ủng hộ giảm vai trò chứ chưa chứng minh nên bỏ thi.
outline.content: Supporters argue that broader assessment can recognise abilities that timed examinations capture poorly. Opponents respond that teacher judgement can vary between schools and may favour pupils with substantial help at home. I favour broader assessment because examinations miss sustained inquiry, but opponents are right that common tests and external moderation remain necessary to make results credible across schools.

paragraphs: Supporters argue that broader assessment can recognise abilities that timed examinations capture poorly. Opponents respond that teacher judgement can vary between schools and may favour pupils with substantial help at home. I favour broader assessment because examinations miss sustained inquiry, but opponents are right that common tests and external moderation remain necessary to make results credible across schools.

Broader assessment can recognise abilities that timed examinations capture poorly. Extended projects reveal how students investigate evidence, revise arguments and manage sustained work. A research project can show the reasoning behind an answer rather than reward the final answer alone. Showing successive drafts allows an assessor to see how an argument improves, rather than infer the entire learning process from a timed final response. A project reveals more about the learning process only if teachers can establish that the investigation and revisions are substantially the pupil's own work.

Teacher judgement can vary between schools and may favour pupils with substantial help at home. Schools differ in the standards teachers apply and in the support families can provide outside lessons. A project grade may consequently reflect the institution or household surrounding a pupil as well as the quality of that pupil's own work. External moderation and some common examinations should support a wider assessment system. Moderation provides a common reference for teacher judgements, while retained examinations can help check whether project grades reflect pupils' independent capabilities. Reform should balance the range of abilities recognised against the reliability and comparability of the grades awarded across different schools.

Supporters make the stronger case for measuring a wider range of achievement, while opponents identify the standardisation that such reform needs; reducing examination dominance should therefore preserve independent checks on comparative performance.
